key_insight: UR-VC shows that demo time is a noisy stand-in for real task progress, and it can be corrected without manual labels. By learning to adjust these time-derived proxies, robots get more reliable progress/value signals for training and completion detection.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of dense, scalable supervision for robot learning. It tackles the mismatch between normalized demonstration time and true physical progress, especially in contact-rich manipulation where actions do not align neatly with time.
method: Uses normalized demonstration time as an initial progress/value proxy.
Learns an unsupervised correction mechanism to reduce proxy noise and better align labels with actual task progress.
Applies the corrected values to improve intermediate state evaluation, policy learning, and task completion detection.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reduces dependence on expensive dense annotations while making robot learning signals more trustworthy. It can improve training stability and downstream performance in real-world manipulation tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: demo video frames -> noisy time proxy -> corrected value signal -> robot policy

paper_title: UR-VC: Unsupervised Robotic Value Correction for Time-Derived Progress Proxies
paper_authors: Lirui Zhao, Modi Shi, Li Chen, Qi Liu, Ping Luo
